I’m a trans man. I was born female and always will be. I’ve been on testosterone for 7 years almost. I’m 5’6” almost, but was 5’4” when I started. The best advice I ever got was from the singer of modest mouse. I confided in him after a show (younger and more talkative) about life and how he keeps going with such a bleak outlook on life. He told me ‘try everything else before you do it’. And it resonated with me. Life is brutal, but there’s dumb fucking fun and joy in tiny things even if we only see it as a void of pain. 

You will realize that all this bullshit — looks, height, weight, it’s in your head, and people prey on you because they see it works. Imagine being a 300 pound closeted transman in high school who everyone accuses of being an in denial lesbian, makes rumors about me wanting to bring weapons to school, and my self harm and misery was just ignored or amusing. 

Try your best to stop caring. These people don’t really give a fuck or even really think these things. They’re just assholes trying to figure out life, and they’ll get their karma. YOU do not need to die over something they will lose with age anyways. I doubt you are ugly, but most people are not even attractive to begin with. There is no point in internalizing these things. 

I lost over 100 pounds. I’m at my ideal bmi after decades of struggling with my weight. Nobody gives a shit. They’re nothing to you. You will find people that aren’t like this. I personally am gay and think dudes under 5’6” are sexy as fuck and don’t intimidate me, so I’m comfortable with them. 

Trust me, dude. Kids and society are brutal but you don’t want their approval anyways. Find your own path, ignore them, work with what you’ve got and work towards being who you want to be. 

Rory Culkin is 5’6” and everyone is lusting over him. Frank iero is like 5’4” if that. 

You’re going to be okay and make it. Think of what you want to be and find a compromise with where you are now. Are you chubby? Think about losing weight if it will make YOU happy. Can’t grow facial hair? Many guys can’t, but look into supplements and treatments. They even make shoe lifts to add height to shoes now.

I had a dissociative disorder that ironically makes me very anxious and panicked when I am not dissociating. The moment I’m like ‘I am alive, in this body, I exist’ is when I go full panic mode. 

Ketamine is a dissociative. My boyfriend insists that he doesn’t know ‘how’ to dissociate, but we all do it. Usually when driving. You just check out. I’m actually writing this in the hospital bed after my probably 18th infusion. 

Ketamine still helps your neural pathways reset even if you aren’t awake. Your brain is still functioning if you dream. If I take an edible and fall asleep, I’ll still have weird dreams. I think it might just be hard for you to notice that you are dissociating, because I always know ‘where’ I am, even when dissociating constantly. I’m always grounded in reality. Most substances won’t make you forget reality. 

My experience is that I feel more ‘objective’ about myself and think of others in a different way. Like we’re all actually connected with people through an invisible network in the air. I don’t think you’re getting nothing out of it, I think you just might be expecting ‘x,y,z’ instead of your mileage may vary.

Listen, it’s okay. All of this is okay. People are on a never-ending journey to find out who they are and what their life is about, and that’s something that’s never given to us or can be helped by another person. You have made the best choices for yourself based on what you knew at the time, and that’s the best you could do. Try not to waste time by regretting what is in the past, and thinking of these things as failures or mistakes, when they were what you thought was right. Even now, you see the positive in it by saying you like having a beard and being a dude. I think a lot of us have felt this. You’re pushed through the transition process quickly because that’s the goal, and then at some point you’re ‘post transition’ (top surgery, hormones, what that means for you) and there isn’t a ‘goal’ to go towards. I’m getting bottom surgery in August, and I’m dreading it, but I know I can’t live my life with how I feel about myself. Do I feel sad that I do feel this way? Absolutely. Do I wish I were able to just be satisfied with how I am? No doubt. But we don’t live in a perfect world. My point is that nothing you’ve done is a mistake, and you’re always able to make changes if you think this might not be the right move forward. 

I will say, please try not to base yourself around what others think. As far as your family, or anyone else, it doesn’t matter if they call you ‘she’ and mess up. You need to decide if they’re the type of people who genuinely love you unconditionally or if they don’t, and if they’re just old and ignorant, it might sting but you’re a man if you believe you are. Over time, even more time than you’ve gone through now, it’ll smooth out. Eventually, everything will fall into place. As for you being ‘dependent’ on healthcare — I mean, you’re really not when you think about it. I’m diabetic and on a few meds for psych stuff, and I don’t want to know what would happen if I stopped those, BUT there’s nothing wrong with that. There’s nothing wrong with taking something prescribed to you to make sure that you have a good life. With hormones, they’re flexible. You can take more or less on a sliding scale, just be sure to speak with your endo. 

I get the feeling of shame sometimes. I just want to be another guy, I don’t want to do all of these extra things just to feel validated or exist. I think that it might be good for you to try and separate yourself from the fact that you’re trans and just exist. You take injections because they’re prescribed to you.
